description.narrative:
This Emergency Appeal responds to the refugee crisis caused by drought and famine in Somalia. In Somalia, the drought and ongoing conflict has reached a crisis level affecting over half of the population, and resulting in more than 250,000 Somalis leaving the country in 2011 alone in search of assistance. The resulting mass movement of rural Somalis to urban areas and across the border to Kenya and Ethiopia to seek relief in a relatively secure environment has put significant pressure on the already overcrowded refugee camps in Kenya. To contribute to improving the situation of refugees in these camps, Catholic Relief Services Kenya developed this two-year intervention. Caritas Internationalis is now launching this Appeal as a fourteen-month emergency response project (twelve months implementation, plus two months for preparation of final reports and audit), and we foresee the launch of a second Appeal for Year Two. The Refugee Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) Project will help drought-affected refugees in Kambioos Camp in Dabaab, Kenya to meet their immediate sanitation, hygiene, and water needs.
CRS Kenya will meet the needs of 12,000 newly arrived refugee households (or 48,000 people, approximately 53% of the anticipated 90,000 population) who are currently in the process of relocating into Kambioos Camp by:
-providing latrines/showers with hand-washing facilities,
-promoting camp hygiene and sanitation with hygiene education and NFI hygiene kits for 12,000 households,
-supporting solid waste disposal management and water drainage,
-planning a contingency water supply as a back up to current plans, and
-Ensuring its activities are accountable to the people it is serving.
By implementing the above activities, CRS envisions the following results:
-Drought-affected refugees use sanitation facilities and services daily
-Drought-affected refugees demonstrate key hygiene behaviours for hand-washing, water handling, and latrine use
-Drought-affected refugees actively engage in the response
-Drought-affected refugees have safe and sufficient water for household use
